# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-low

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Two cooperating agents (one per feature, with messaging and a shared git remote) run on the 50-pair `flash` subset with the exact same per-agent setup as [`solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-low`](../solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-low/summary.md): `gemini-3.8-flash` at `low` thinking, 500 steps, compaction at 64K tokens, the per-turn step counter, and a `$40` per-agent cost cap. Comparing each pair against the `solo` saturation runs (`36/50` at `low`, `37/50` across `low` and `high`) separates coordination failures from single-agent capability limits on a 50-pair sample. It ran as two 25-pair halves on two API keys and was merged into this one run.

## Observations

- 30/50 (60%) for `$39.85`, down 6 pairs (12 percentage points) from `solo` with the same setup (`36/50`, 72%, `$25.70`). Every pair `coop --git` passed was also passed by `solo` at `low` thinking (`0` wins over `solo`, `6` losses: `pallets_click_task/2068` (6,7) and (7,10), `pallets_click_task/2800` (2,7), `pallets_click_task/2956` (1,8), `pallets_jinja_task/1621` (4,5), and `pillow_task/290` (3,5)). Against the 37 pairs solved by `solo` at `low` or `high`, `coop --git` retained 30/37 (81%).
- Neither step limits nor text merge conflicts caused the drop. All 100 agents submitted before the 500-step limit (median 87 steps, max 186, median 0 compactions), and all 50 pairs merged without conflicts (43 clean three-way merges and 7 identical pre-merged branches). Agents exchanged 12 to 66 messages per pair (median 28).
- In all 6 losses on `solo`-solvable pairs, one feature passed and the other failed after a clean merge. On two of them (`pallets_click_task/2068` (6,7) and (7,10)), avoiding a git conflict directly caused the bug: both features needed to pass a new option into the same constructor call, and the agents agreed in chat to leave that call line untouched and attach their setting on the class or instance afterward so `git merge` would not conflict. Their trial merges and self-written tests passed, and the hidden tests failed when checking the constructor arguments.
- On the other 4 losses (`pallets_click_task/2800` (2,7), `pallets_click_task/2956` (1,8), `pallets_jinja_task/1621` (4,5), and `pillow_task/290` (3,5)), each peer checked that `git merge` had no conflicts and that existing plus self-written tests passed, missing edge-case or state-handling bugs in one feature (such as clearing an exit callback after first use or not updating a wrapper palette object) that the `solo` agent got right.
